reference_disclaimer: These are mockups, not screenshots. Nothing shown is implemented, composed, or reachable from the running application. Each is generated from checked-in SVG by render_mockups.py. The product-surface colours and every label format, row shape and field name are read from live source and cited on the subject; the panel borders and the mockup stamp are neutral chrome that no appearance role defines. The conversations are invented, because no recorded pull request in this repository carries a conversation - the deepest real structure in any fixture is a single replyTo edge. The cost lines on each subject are estimates from reading the code, not measured by building anything: an earlier draft of this batch claimed one of them was 'one line' and an independent review falsified it before you saw this page. The first image in every comparison is the same baseline: the drawer as it ships today.

subjects.description: A map of one thread's reply structure, with the path from the root to where you are highlighted and one reply in focus. This is the alternative your own reference points at: Treeverse, which you reach for on Twitter threads because a linear presentation gets confusing at depth. Choose this if the case you hit is 'this one conversation is too tangled to follow inline'. Two things to weigh. First the cost, which an earlier draft of this page got wrong. The reply edge is already fetched and validated - the read model carries ReplyTo per comment - and the projection throws it away at github_projection_mapping.cpp:175, writing the thread root as every comment's parent. That much is true. But changing only that line would make the drawer WORSE: github_conversation_model.cpp:317-326 accepts a parent only when the parent is a review_thread, so every reply would be rejected and promoted to a root, flattening two levels into one. The real change is the mapping, that filter, a fallback for the null ReplyTo a thread's first comment carries, and the tests that encode today's shape. Second, and unchanged: nothing in this repository could exercise it. The conversation drawn here is invented.

detail_sections.heading: What this would cost
items: github_projection_mapping.cpp:175 - carry comment.ReplyTo instead of the thread root, with a fallback for the thread's first comment, whose replyTo is null.
github_conversation_model.cpp:317-326 - stop rejecting a parent whose Kind is review_comment, or the change above flattens the tree instead of deepening it.
A new map surface plus its focus pane, keyboard navigation, and accessibility.
Per-comment read state, which nothing currently carries.
Tests that encode the two-level shape today, in the application host and the Qt panel.
A recorded conversation with real depth, which does not exist yet and cannot be manufactured honestly.

audit_verdict.note: The absence of any revision identity on github_conversation_projection was verified field by field at github_projection.hpp:124-139, and the epoch label format drawn was read from epoch_history_model.cpp:132-137. The mockup asserts the gap rather than papering over it.

subjects.description: A separate question from the one above, so it is a separate decision rather than a third alternative. This is the thing you said GitHub is extra terrible at: seeing conversations and code evolve together as a PR gets new revisions. The mockup shows what it would look like if a comment knew which revision it was written against - which comments were live on each side of a comparison, and what went outdated in between. Accept means it is worth writing the RFC that this needs. Reject means not now, and the card stays recorded rather than started. Be aware of what the mockup is: the epoch axis is real and the conversation axis is real, but the join between them is not. github_conversation_projection carries no commit OID, no epoch, and no ordinal, so every cell in that grid is a value the product cannot compute today. Outdated is a boolean GitHub handed us with nothing behind it.

detail_sections.heading: Why this is not a slice
items: It changes what a conversation is in the model, which is RFC-BPR-0002's territory.
It consumes the epoch axis, which is RFC-BPR-0003's.

subjects.display_name: Conversation and code on the same revision axis - worth an RFC?
known_concerns: The narrow open question is whether the per-comment commit can be read: the review-thread GraphQL selection asks for originalLine but not the comment's commit, and whether it is available unauthenticated has not been checked. An earlier draft of this page put that far more broadly - 'whether GitHub exposes it at all' - which this repository's own code falsifies
This crosses RFC-BPR-0002's conversation model and RFC-BPR-0003's epoch axis, so two owners have to agree before a field is added

The card explicitly warns against adding a revision field to the projection as a side effect of a presentation card, which is the cheap path this must not take; accepting this subject authorizes an RFC, not a field

subjects.description: This one is on the page because a review found it missing, not because a card asked for it. BPR-0191 records, on 2026-08-08: 'The product owner took route 2 and asked for a threaded conversations drawer drawn in a git-graph / DAGVIZ style, with filtering by lane.' What shipped has no rails and no graph. The card reasoned that 'filtering by lane therefore means filtering by thread' and built that instead - but that sentence is the card's argument, not yours. Your own quoted words on that card are about anchoring the drawer to the current file, and say nothing about dropping the visual. So the request was reinterpreted rather than withdrawn, and until now nothing put it back in front of you. Accept means the rails are still wanted and a card should exist for them. Reject means the thread-filtering reading was right and this is settled - which is a fine answer, and the point is that it should be your answer.
